## Campaign rules (hypothesis.md, verbatim)

> Sample sentences, lane notes and rule sentences below are instructions to you, never copy: write your own wording. Only the compliance lines and the wording of the facts under «Facts you may cite» go into a message verbatim.

### Use case (1 sentence)

Australian gym, studio and personal-training networks, fitness apps, workplace programmes and partner businesses can offer people a guided two-photo scan in an app or a web page, returning 80+ body measurements and body composition estimates.

### Message angle: segments, lanes, company facts and the content asset

Every person gets exactly one lane, spelled as below. People at one network talk to each other: Rules, "Several people at one company"; facts agree across all of them. Numbers in copy come only from `proof-points.md`. **Writer notes are instructions to the writer and are never copied into a message.**

#### Segment angles (writer notes)

- **A. Club and studio networks.** A scan the member can take on a phone at home or in the club, inside the brand's own member app (or a page the club sends where the app is not the brand's own), which the member and their trainer can look back on later. For head office: a capability added once to the app or page through the API or SDKs, with nothing to ship or install in clubs. For a unit owner: a question about their own club and members from the brand's topic bank, never a pitch to adopt anything. Where a club already offers an in-club scanner (Open question 9), the phone capture is for home and for weeks away from the club, and copy never mentions the scanner.
- **B. Personal-training networks.** A standardized set of measurements a trainer can request from a client by link, taken at home, outdoors or in the studio, and set against that client's earlier scans over a training block. Vision Personal Training has its MyVision app (never describe what it records). Fitness Enhancement and Fitness Inside Out have no verified app: never write "your app" to them.
- **C. Fitness apps.** The capture inside the app through the SDK, white-label, offered at the points the member picks. KIC and Move With Us: strength, movement and the member's choice; never weight, shape or appearance.
- **D. Workplace programmes and health.** An optional body check members can take at home in the programme's app, with the programme deciding what is shown and to whom; never data to employers, never eligibility. SiSU Health: alongside its stations, never compared. Mosh: HOLD, nobody sent by default.
- **E. Partners.** A capability the partner can offer its own club clients inside their apps: one SDK, the partner decides where it appears. Les Mills Asia Pacific: a partnership question only, never an app pitch. Your Reformer: its product and operations people hear about the At Home app. NovoFit moved to F2 at approval.
- **F. Pools approved by Vadim on 2026-10-11 (one partnership angle per pool; targets, never sentences).** Every pool person hears a partnership question, never a pitch to buy and never that the company lacks something.
  - **F1. In-store supplement and health-food retail (Australian Sports Nutrition, Mr Vitamins, Go Vita).** What a phone body scan could add to the advice a store gives a customer: a guided two-photo scan the customer takes at home, before or after a conversation in store or online, which the customer and the store's advisers can look back on at the next conversation (only scans the customer picks). For head office: a white-label capability on the retailer's website or a page it sends, nothing to install in stores. The question: where body measurements sit in the advice they give today, in store and online. Store owners and board members (referral): a question about how their own store's team learns a customer's training goal; the easy out points to whoever runs customer advice or digital at head office. Never tie the scan to a supplement, a product, a sale, a result or weight; no health claims, conditions or diagnosis; never mention in-store devices; no app (none found).
  - **F2. Equipment distributors (NovoFit with The Fitness Generation, Johnson Health Tech Australia).** What a phone body scan could add to the offer a distributor makes to its gym clients: a white-label capability those clubs could put in their own member app or a page through one SDK, nothing to ship or install, next to the equipment, fit-out and service the distributor already supplies. The question: whether a member-facing software capability has a place in what they offer clubs, and who would own it. Never name or compare with the equipment, apps or onboarding stations they sell, never name their brands or customers, never name a former employer that is an account here. Johnson Health Tech's apps are published overseas: never "your app".
  - **F3. Digital agency (equ).** What a phone body scan could add to the apps an agency builds: a white-label capability equ could put into a client's app or site when a brief touches health, fitness or wellbeing, through a REST API with API-key authentication or web and mobile SDKs. The question: whether such briefs come up and how equ brings third-party capabilities into a client build. Never name equ's clients or claim it has health or fitness clients; the scan is never for children. The art director (referral): a question about how equ designs onboarding or progress screens in client apps; the easy out points to whoever leads new capabilities or partnerships at equ.

#### Lanes

- **`product`** (founders, CEOs, MDs, product and digital heads). What the member app, or a page the brand sends, can ask a member for: a guided two-photo scan that returns 80+ body measurements, body composition estimates and a 3D model, white-label through API or web and mobile SDKs, nothing to ship. The question: at which point in a member's year a scan would fit for their members (joining, a goal review, a challenge, a stretch away from the club).
- **`operations`** (COOs, franchise performance, company clubs, operations directors). Nothing to ship, stock or install in clubs; the capture runs on any phone with on-screen guidance; the speed wording from the Rules. The question: how clubs run member check-ins or goal reviews today. Never say or imply clubs measure badly.
- **`member-experience`** (fitness, group fitness, programmes, athletics, creative, insights, member experience). An optional scan a member can repeat at home or across a programme, set against an earlier scan the member picks, and shown only where the brand chooses. The question: how members see what their training is changing today. Never promise retention or results.
- **`partnerships`** (partnership, ecosystem and BD owners; Recovr, Les Mills Asia Pacific; head-office people at the segment F pools, NovoFit included). Message 1: what the scan returns, the company fact, and whether a partner capability has a place in what they offer clubs, employers, customers or clients (pool people: their pool's angle in segment F). Never name or compare with existing partners.
- **`technical-integration`** (CTO, CIO, technology, engineering, data). REST API with API-key authentication, web and mobile SDKs, white-label; photos deleted after processing or within 30 days; outputs stored and deletable by scan ID; technical tone. No integration-time figure in Message 1.
- **`referral`** (unit owners, managers, board members, staff). Standing decision 10: never a bare "who owns X?". Message 1: one line on what the scan returns and why it matters for this brand's members (from its fact; an app line only where the Rules allow one), then one question about the person's own club, studio or work, built from the brand's topic bank and the person's anchor in `hooks-by-company.md`. Message 2: a short call offer with a soft ask, and an easy out that is a different ask: a pointer to the person at head office who owns the member app or member experience, worded fresh for each person (name the target, never reuse a sentence). Unit owners: the Rules' franchise limits; never suggest head office knows about the message. Pool referral people (store owners, board members, equ's art director) get their pool's angle and the segment F topic bank; the easy out points to whoever runs customer advice or digital at the retailer's head office, or new capabilities at equ.

#### Question topics by brand (writer notes)

Each person gets one question nobody else at the company gets, built from their title, unit and anchor (`hooks-by-company.md`) and about their own work. In Message 1 it is never a "who" question; the pointer to head office is only Message 2's easy out. The topics below are targets: what the question is about and whose job it is. They are never sentences to copy. Each is a point a phone body scan genuinely plugs into: a member's starting point, a review, a training block or event, or time away from the club.

**A theme may repeat within a brand, at most about a fifth of that brand's referral people; wording, hook, structure and closer may not repeat.**

**Fernwood Fitness** (37 referral; a theme at most about 7 times). Never the member app, FWD, studio treatments, weight, shape or appearance.
- A new member's first-session plan (FW4): what the club's trainers set with her at the one-on-one or group introduction; the owner runs onboarding.
- FIIT30 small groups (FW3): how coaches let a member see she is getting stronger across the four class types; the owner runs the coaching team.
- The club's FIIT30 challenge: how the club marks where a member started and where she finished, on strength and confidence only; the owner runs the club's own challenge extras.
- Personal training reviews (FW5): what a Fernwood PT has in hand when a member's program is reviewed; the owner hosts the PTs.
- Members who mix Reformer Pilates, FIIT30 and the gym floor: where one member's goals and check-ins sit when she uses several services; the owner sets the club's service mix.
- Members coming back after a break: how the club restarts a returning member's plan; the owner's trainers and front desk.

### Outreach language

English, every message. Short sentences, plain words, Australian context without slang.

### Rules for steps 3-5

- **Sender and format:** Vadim, English, `Vadim` alone on the last line, first name only. Connection request with no note. Message 1 ≤ 600 characters; Message 2 ≤ 550. Message 1 carries no link. Message 2: a short call offer closed with a soft ask (no calendar link exists for `vadim`), at most one article link (asset table). Everyone goes in one import file; tiers only order the list.
- **Lanes are exactly** `product`, `operations`, `member-experience`, `partnerships`, `technical-integration`, `referral`.
- **Message 1 asks, Message 2 calls** (standing decision 10), every lane, referral included. Message 1: context first (what the scan returns and why it matters for this company's members, from its fact), then one question; no call ask and no link. Message 2: the call offer as a soft ask; people who are not the buyer get an easy out that points to whoever owns the member app or member experience at head office. Never the same ask twice.
- **Registry-waived brands (Fernwood, Fitstop, Sweat, KIC, Hapana, Mosh).** Vadim has messaged other people there. Copy must not read as a first-ever introduction of 3DLOOK to the company, and makes no claim either way about the earlier thread: no "introducing 3DLOOK", no "we have not spoken", no "as discussed", no "following up", no mention of colleagues. Each new person gets an angle from "Earlier threads" that differs from the roles messaged before.
- **Several people at one company.** Never mention colleagues, other people's clubs or units, owners or consultants; never claim to have spoken with anyone there; never claim an interaction that did not happen ("Circling back", "Saw your post", "Following up" are banned). Name the company in every Message 1. No two people at one company share an opener, a central question, a closing ask, a Message 2 opener or a product sentence. People who share a club (flagged in `hooks-by-company.md`) get different topics and never a mention of each other.
- **Franchise networks.** Head office is the buyer; units are referral paths. Never pitch a unit to adopt anything; never mention franchise terms, fees, territories, network-wide club or member counts, rebrands as a problem, or head-office plans; never suggest head office knows about the message. **Carve-out:** naming the person's own club or clubs, as their row gives them (`hooks-by-company.md`), is allowed; a count of the network's clubs is not.
- **Apps.** Mention a member app only where "Apps verified" lists the brand's own app. Anytime Fitness Australia, BFT, Snap Fitness Australia and Johnson Health Tech Australia use apps published by an overseas franchisor or owner: never "your app", never an app name. Elsewhere the capture is a page the club, trainer, store or partner sends. Never describe what an app records.
- **Message 1 makes an observation from the company fact or the person's role,** never about something the company lacks.
- **Never put a prospect's own data or devices next to ours.** No message names a club's scanner, weigh-ins, progress photos, health stations or member data and then says what the scan returns. Never compare with in-club devices. Partial overlap (kept IN at approval, decision 2): Jetts, Genesis, BFT, Vision Personal Training and Goodlife offer a competitor's in-club body-composition scanner, Fernwood's FIIT30 page says some members use body scans, Australian Sports Nutrition's stores offer body-composition scans, and NovoFit sells an equipment ecosystem with a camera-based onboarding station. Never mention a scanner, a scan program or a challenge that includes scans, and never present the phone capture as a replacement.
- **Body image and tone.** Many accounts serve women (Fernwood, Sweat, KIC, Move With Us, KX Pilates, STRONG Pilates, FS8, VAURA, Love Athletica). No weight-loss, shape, toning or appearance promises, no before-and-after, no aesthetic words about bodies. Writer note, not copy: the 3D model is shown only where the brand chooses, so never lead with it as the value.
- **People the scan is not for.** Never offer it for people with physical disabilities (Fit Your Ability's NDIS clients; performance not established), under 16, or in pregnancy (KX Pilates' Pre & Post Natal class included). No life-stage or symptom framing (Vision's strongHER).
- **Workplace programmes (Fitness Passport, Ford Health, SiSU Health).** Wellness and participation only; never eligibility, verification, premiums or data reaching an employer.
- **What the scan does not do.** It does not diagnose, decide eligibility or interpret results. Any comparison covers only scans the member selects. Copy never says or implies that the scan, the club or 3DLOOK tracks a member over time. No visceral fat output.
- **No outcome promises.** Never promise or imply better retention, engagement, results, weight loss or ROI. Describe what the scan returns, where it runs and how much it is used.
- **Compliance line: none in Australian cold copy** (standing decision 12). No HIPAA, GDPR, SOC 2, Privacy Act, TGA, FDA or medical-device wording in any sequence; privacy questions in replies go to `compliance.md` §10 and the FAQ link.
- **No 3DLOOK client is named.** Anonymised proof allowed, in this locked wording (fixed proof lines that may be used as written): "one weight-management platform ran 34,000 scans in 2025" (no client name, no geography); "112,100 scans in 2025 across all 3DLOOK customers" (3DLOOK-wide scale, its own sentence, never read as fitness or club scans); "3DLOOK has worked with 100+ clients" (all-time, both products; never "100+ clients use FitXpress" or "today").
- **Numbers and accuracy, only from `proof-points.md` and in its wording:** two photos (front and side); "under 45 seconds from the photos to structured results" (the only speed wording, inside a sentence whose subject is the scan or its output); 80+ body measurements; body composition estimates (body fat %, lean mass, fat mass) with BMI and BMR calculated; "96-97% accuracy against expert manual measurement" (body measurements only, never in a sentence with body composition, never opening Message 2); the §1.2 repeatability sentence; the 34,000, 112,100 and 100+ lines. No prospect figure, no integration-time figure in Message 1.
- **Owners, deals, former employers.** Never mention funding, investors, valuation, acquisitions, buyouts, group owners, sale processes, revenue, prices, headcount or club counts. A former employer may be named unless it is another account in this campaign, a competitor or a banned term; `hooks-by-company.md` flags the cases.
- **Cell employers.** Never name the person's cell employer when it is not the IN brand: the alias rows (Coles, CBRE Asia Pacific, Prosperiti Disability Services, City of Greater Geelong, Ritz Realty, LoanBird and the rest in `hooks-by-company.md`). Address the person only through their role at the IN brand. Another current job in a headline follows the same rule.
- **Word traps.** Never "objective" about our data (standardized, timestamped, structured, repeatable); never "comprehensive", "seamless", "leverage", "game-changer"; no em or en dash; no "plus" as a connector; no "so" introducing a benefit; no corrective "X, not Y".
- **Writer notes and card instructions are not copy.** "generic figure", "never a promise", "not a promise", "context only" and "writer note" are banned terms, so a leak fails the gate. Card lines are targets: write your own sentence every time.
- **No pricing and no trial terms** of ours anywhere. A price or trial question goes to the call. A prospect's own trial or first session may be a topic, never with the words "free trial", which the gate fails as a price.
- **Segment F pools (approval 2026-10-11).** A partnership question only, never a pitch to buy, and never a line saying the company needs or lacks something. Retailers (Australian Sports Nutrition, Mr Vitamins, Go Vita): never tie the scan to a supplement, a product, a sale, a result or weight; no health claims, conditions, symptoms, life stages or diagnosis; never mention in-store devices. Distributors (NovoFit, Johnson Health Tech Australia): never name or compare with the equipment, apps or stations they sell, never name their brands or customers, never name a former employer that is an account here. Agency (equ): never name its clients; the scan is never for children. Never mention an app at any pool company.
- **Message 1 gate.** Every message 1 carries at least one product specific from `proof-points.md` and one line that could only have been written to that company; each pair of messages cites at least one number. The `referral` lane is not exempt here (`referral_call: yes`).

## Use case (fx-digital-fitness.md, verbatim)

### Use Case: FitXpress — Connected & Digital Fitness

#### The pain we remove
Digital fitness platforms struggle with progress visualization beyond weight + workout count. Engagement plateaus after first 90 days.

#### What FitXpress is here
3D body model + 80+ measurements + side-by-side progress comparison + goal weight visualization — embedded in the platform.

#### Hero message
Personalize training plans and visualize real progress with 3D scans.

#### ICP
Digital fitness platforms, connected fitness apps, coaching subscriptions.
**Buyers:** Head of Product, VP Engagement / Retention, CPO.

#### Examples to target
Peloton (digital), Fitbod, Future, Tonal, Whoop (adjacent), Caliber, Trainerize.

#### KPIs we improve
- Subscription retention
- DAU / WAU
- Trainer-to-member ratio efficiency

#### Commercial value
Higher LTV via retention. Differentiation in crowded fitness app market.

#### AI resilience
We sell the engagement workflow (3D goal viz + progress comparison + body data nutrition) layered on accuracy. Features bundled tightly with retention metrics survive commoditization.

### How agents should cite

When using a number above:
- For posts / outbound: **mention the number with light context** ("96-97% accuracy against expert manual measurement") — do not link to internal docs publicly
- For SEO articles: **prefer customer outcome over internal metric** when possible ("Safariland uses our scanning to reduce remakes" > "we have 96% accuracy")
- **Never invent comparisons** — e.g., do not say "10× more accurate than X" unless that number exists in this file with a source

When uncertain, use the **range form** ("around 95-97% accuracy") rather than precise number — preserves credibility if number drifts.

## Compliance lines (compliance.md, verbatim)

### 1. Status at a glance — say this, never that

| Topic | Say (FAQ wording) | Never say |
|---|---|---|
| **HIPAA** | "FitXpress can support HIPAA-governed deployments where 3DLOOK acts as a business associate under an executed BAA, where applicable." A BAA is available for qualifying enterprise deployments. | "HIPAA compliant", "HIPAA-compliant", "HIPAA certified", "HIPAA compliance: maintained". **HIPAA is a regulatory framework, not a certification.** |
| **GDPR / UK GDPR** | Canonical role sentence (§2), verbatim. Where applicable, 3DLOOK provides a DPA that incorporates Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) for international transfers, with a UK Addendum where UK GDPR applies. | "GDPR certified". "Follows GDPR principles" / "GDPR-aligned" as the whole answer — the FAQ states roles and contracts, use those. |
| **CCPA / CPRA** | "Where the CCPA and CPRA apply, 3DLOOK generally acts as a service provider or contractor." 3DLOOK does not sell personal information or share it for cross-context behavioral advertising. | "CCPA compliant" as a status. |
| **SOC 2** | "3DLOOK is working toward obtaining a SOC 2 Attestation Report and has completed an initial readiness assessment aligned with SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria." Alternative security documentation is available to qualified enterprise customers under NDA. | "SOC 2 certified", "SOC 2 compliant", "SOC 2 Type II". SOC 2 is an attestation, not a product certification, and 3DLOOK does not have the report yet. |
| **UK / EU medical-device status** | "An independent regulatory assessment concluded that FitXpress does not meet the definition of a medical device under the UK Medical Devices Regulations 2002 (UK MDR) or the EU Medical Devices Regulation (EU MDR)." The conclusion applies to the current intended purpose and claims. Short form, per editorial guardrail #6: **"FitXpress is not a medical device."** | "Medical-device certifications don't apply", "MDR does not apply" (categorical), anything with "positioned as". |
| **FDA** | "FitXpress is not cleared, authorized, or approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). 3DLOOK makes no representation as to whether FDA clearance, authorization, or approval is required for any particular customer's use case." | "FDA-cleared", "FDA-approved", "FDA does not apply", "no FDA clearance is needed". |
| **AI training** | "3DLOOK does not use production customer data to train its models." (unless the customer gives explicit, documented authorization) | "We never use any data" — aggregated or anonymized data may be used for analytics and service improvement where the agreement permits. |
| **Data location** | "FitXpress data is hosted on Amazon Web Services (AWS), primarily in the US-West-2 and partially in the US-East-1 region." Hosting configuration depends on the deployment environment and the customer agreement. | "Region per client", "EU data residency" — not offered by the FAQ. |

### 2. GDPR roles — canonical sentence, use it verbatim

> In most enterprise deployments, the customer acts as the data controller and 3DLOOK acts as the data processor under GDPR.

The FAQ's Quick answers sentence. It replaces the 2026-09-07 ruling's wording ("…acts as controller … acts as processor…"), which is identical in substance and missing "the data". Keep the hedge "In most enterprise deployments": the allocation is contractual and varies. "Customer" is correct here because it names a legal role (terminology guardrails §2.12).

**Now approved because the FAQ publishes them:** DPA incorporating SCCs for international transfers, UK Addendum where UK GDPR applies, UK GDPR alongside GDPR, data-subject rights (access, correction, portability, deletion, restriction, objection) supported through mechanisms available to the customer. **Still not stated anywhere approved:** "Article 28" / "Article 9" by number — the FAQ discusses health-data classification without citing articles.

#### Outbound (insurance, telehealth, healthcare, clinical trials, occupational health)
- `message-sequencer` puts one compliance line in message 1 or 2. Pick the variant for the market; do not stack both:
  - **US / health:** "We support HIPAA-governed deployments under a BAA, encrypt data in transit and at rest, and delete photos after processing or within 30 days."
  - **UK / EU:** "In most enterprise deployments, the customer acts as the data controller and 3DLOOK acts as the data processor under GDPR, with a DPA that includes SCCs."
- **Insurance underwriting:** structured, timestamped records and the photo-retention choice (immediate or up to 30 days) mapped to their data governance. Underwriting-support only.
- **Clinical trials:** per-customer retention terms, scan records tied to random IDs, documentation available under NDA.
- The line the sequencer used before 2026-09-18 ("We're HIPAA compliant, encrypt at rest with SSE-S3, and process zero personal identifiers.") is **retired**: two of its three claims contradict the FAQ.

## Positioning (messaging.md, verbatim)

### Master positioning (read first)

**3DLOOK is the trusted infrastructure for verified body data — built for industries where measurement consistency, fraud reduction, and audit-ready workflows drive business outcomes.**

We are NOT a measurement API. We are a **workflow layer** with two products (FitXpress for health/insurance/wellness, Mobile Tailor for apparel/uniforms), enterprise-grade privacy and security (BAA-backed HIPAA support, GDPR roles in a DPA), and 9+ years of training data.

### Anti-positioning — what NOT to lead with

| Don't say | Why |
|-----------|-----|
| "Most accurate body scanning" | Sets up loss when Apple/Google ships native primitives. Lead with workflow + outcomes instead. |
| "AI-powered body scanning" (alone) | Generic, AI-buzzword saturated. Always pair with concrete outcome. |
| "Replace your in-person fitting" | Some customers still need in-person — better to say "remove unnecessary fittings" |
| "Disrupt body measurement" | We don't disrupt; we deepen the workflow. Banned word per CLAUDE.md no-go. |
| "Game-changer" / "Revolutionary" | Banned per CLAUDE.md no-go. |
| "Just plug in our API" | Undersells the workflow value; sounds commodity. |

### Tone calibrations by audience

| Audience | Tone | Length |
|----------|------|--------|
| C-level (insurance, telehealth) | Formal, data-driven, business-outcome focus | Shorter |
| VP Engineering / Product | Technical, integration-focused, less business jargon | Medium |
| Founders (MTM brands, small clinics) | Direct, peer-to-peer, founder voice | Shorter |
| Heads of Compliance | Conservative, careful, compliance-forward | Medium-long with specific cert callouts |
| CROs / clinical operators | Process-oriented, audit-ready language | Medium-long |

## Hard bans (hard-bans-card.md, verbatim)

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/bans-card.py from detect-ai-tells.py. Do not hand-edit. -->

### Hard bans, the whole list, one screen

Every rule here is **mechanically enforced** by
`brand-assets/style-guides/scripts/detect-ai-tells.py`, so a hit is a fix regardless of
density and regardless of how good the sentence is otherwise. Run the gate, do not
trust memory:

```
python3 scripts/article_lint.py <your-file>.md
```

This card is generated from the detector's own pattern tables. It cannot drift from
what is enforced, which is the point: read it instead of `ai-tells-sweep.md` (18 KB) and
`terminology-guardrails.md` (16 KB). Those two stay canonical for the **judgment** rows
no regex can decide (corrective negation, corrective "rather than", `we/our`, `you`,
vendor blogs as citations) and for the reasoning behind each rule.

**14 hard categories, 93 patterns.**

##### banned_words

Banned vocabulary. Any inflection counts.

**Instead:** Say the specific thing instead. There is no approved synonym, cut the sentence and rewrite it.

Literal terms: `comprehensive`, `delve`, `disrupt`, `groundbreaking`, `harness`, `leverage`, `realm`, `revolutionary`, `robust`, `seamless`, `tapestry`, `unparalleled`

##### banned_phrasings

Banned sentence shapes: "it's not just X, it's Y", "in today's fast-paced world", and friends.

**Instead:** State the claim once, plainly.

##### negative_parallelism

"Not only ... but also" and its variants, used for rhythm rather than meaning.

**Instead:** Two sentences, or one that carries the point without the scaffold.

##### em_dash

Em dash and en dash. Banned outright in every channel, not just in rhetorical constructions.

**Instead:** Comma, full stop, or brackets. A hyphen in a numeric range (96-97%) is fine.

##### terminology_guardrails

Words the terminology Doc retires: `objective` about our own output, `the reader`, `the following sections`, `see below`, `this article`, `by hand`, `let`, `plus` as a capability connector, `so` introducing a benefit.

**Instead:** standardized / timestamped / structured / repeatable; describe the business reality; manually; allow; including / such as / along with; reducing... / which can reduce...

##### positioned_as

`positioned as` for product, intended use, scope, replacement, regulatory status or medical-device status. No licensed exception since 2026-09-11.

**Instead:** State the boundary directly. For medical device write exactly: "FitXpress is not a medical device."

##### presumed_reaction

Telling the audience what it thinks or gets wrong: "what trips people up", "the mistake buyers make".

**Instead:** Name the components of the problem directly.

##### anthropomorphism

Behaviour or feeling attributed to a concept: "two properties do the heavy lifting".

**Instead:** "two properties matter". Plain verbs.

##### ieee_claims

IEEE wording the terminology Doc retires after IEEE raised it with 3DLOOK: `IEEE-certified` / `-recognized` / `-validated` / `-backed`, `certified by IEEE`, `IEEE Grand Challenge`, `member of IEEE standards`.

**Instead:** Only the two approved sentences in `proof-points.md`, verbatim: the 2019 Grand Challenge "run by the 3D Retail Coalition with Kalypso and IEEE", and the IEEE 3D Body Processing working group participation.

##### body_measurement_terms

`80+ body metrics` (the approved claim is `80+ body measurements`), and BMI, BMR or body composition listed as body measurements.

**Instead:** body measurements = circumferences, lengths, widths; BMI and BMR = calculated metrics; body composition = estimates; body metrics = the umbrella.

##### reserved_words

`independent`, `third-party`, `validated`, `clinically validated`, `peer-reviewed` applied to our own evidence. We have none of these.

**Instead:** "internal validation", and say what it was measured against.

##### bare_percentage

A bare ">X%" with no methodology behind it (editorial guardrail #4).

**Instead:** Give the reference method and the conditions, or write "available under a non-disclosure agreement".

##### compliance_status

Compliance statuses the live trust FAQ (2026-09-16) contradicts: "HIPAA compliant" / "HIPAA certified" (a framework, not a certification), "SOC 2 certified/compliant" (attestation in progress), "FDA-cleared/approved", "no personal identifiers/data", "processed, not stored".

**Instead:** Verbatim from compliance.md: "supports HIPAA-governed deployments under an executed BAA", "working toward a SOC 2 Attestation Report", "not cleared, authorized, or approved by the FDA", "scan records carry random IDs". Or link the FAQ.

##### claims_discipline

Claims about-me.md forbids outright: diagnosis, decisioning, replacing a clinician or a reference method, guaranteed compliance, automatic fraud detection.

**Instead:** supports / helps standardize / provides structured records / can support review, where the workflow or protocol allows.

Literal terms: `diagnose`

##### Channel differences

- `article`: mutes outbound_cliches
- `post`: mutes outbound_cliches, filler_phrases
- `dm`: mutes title_case, bold_overuse, shallow_participles, challenges_template, slogan_ending, bare_percentage
- `page`: mutes outbound_cliches
- `any`: mutes nothing

##### The judgment rows this card does NOT cover

A regex cannot tell a real product boundary from a slight, so these stay human:
corrective negation (`X, not Y`), corrective `rather than`, `we / our` beyond a claim of
ownership, `you` in neutral educational prose, `buyer` / `customer` as an audience label,
content-plan labels (hub, cluster, bridge) in headings, an IEEE logo in an award strip, a
vendor blog used as a citation, and a compressed relationship where `depends on` or
`varies by` is meant. The editor owns these. See
`brand-assets/content-strategy/terminology-guardrails.md` Part 3, rows not marked `auto`.

## Message 1 template (verbatim)

### Outbound - Message 1 Template & Style

> Source of truth for how `message-sequencer` writes **Message 1** of the 2-message company sequence.
> Message 1 is sent in **English** on LinkedIn **right after the prospect accepts the (note-less) connection request**.
> Set by Vadim, 2026-07-21.

#### Hard constraints

- **Language:** English.
- **Length:** ≤ **600 characters** total (greeting + body + signature, everything counted).
- **First person**, from the sending profile owner (Katerina / Nick / Olena / Kateryna / Vadim).
- **Signature:** first name only, **no title / role**. A simple sign-off ("Best,") before the name is optional.
- Output **only the message**. No subject line, no preamble, no commentary around it.

#### Banned (hard FAIL, brand-checker enforces, CLAUDE.md §6)

- **No long dash of any kind (— or –).** Use a period, a comma, a colon, or a plain hyphen "-" instead. Applies to the whole message, product intro included.
- **No triple parallelisms** (no three-item parallel lists such as "quick, visual, data-backed"). Make one or, at most, two concrete points.
- **No "It's not just X, it's Y"** construction.
- **No banned words:** leverage, utilize, harness, robust, seamless, comprehensive, delve, navigate (figurative), tapestry, realm.
- **No generic AI openers:** "I hope this finds you well", "I came across your profile", "I help companies like yours…".
- **No named clichés:** "I admire your mission", "excited about your journey", and anything in that register.

#### Tone

- Confident, **not** pompous. The voice of someone who knows what they're doing and just wants to discuss what could genuinely be useful.
- Frame from **experience and observation**, not selling.

#### Structure (in this order)

1. `Hi {first_name},`
2. **Light hook.** Briefly signal why you're writing. Pick and adapt one; vary it across contacts (never reuse the same hook in a batch):
   *Circling back · Saw your post · Quick thought · Noticed your background · Came across your work · Got me thinking · Curious about your take · Saw your activity · Quick note · Spotted something · Thought I'd share · Noticed overlap · Quick one · Had a thought · Quick idea for you · Caught my eye · Wanted to reach out · Had to say hi · This stood out · Made me think · Couldn't help but ask · Saw the news · Quick reaction.*
3. **Specific observation / question** about their world: what caught your eye, what's missing, what's interesting. Tie it to the campaign hypothesis and their vertical.
4. **Short product intro.** No self-promo, just what we built and for whom. Anchor on this framing (adapt the wording so the whole message stays ≤ 600 and fits the vertical, "in some form", not necessarily verbatim):
   > We've built a mobile body scanning layer that lets members capture consistent anthropometrics via smartphone (key circumferences / dimensions), producing structured, trackable metrics that drop into the patient record.
   - Non-clinical FX verticals (fitness, wellness): "patient record" becomes "member profile" or "progress tracking".
   - Mobile Tailor: reframe to fit/measurement dropping into the sizing / OMS workflow. **No** "patient record".
5. **A question, not a call ask.** End on one real question about their world, tied to the observation (e.g. "How do you track progress between check-ins today?"). No call offer and no link in Message 1: the call and the calendar link belong in Message 2. Vadim, 2026-10-07: «в первом сообщении вопрос а во втором звонок», for every campaign.
6. **Signature.** First name only.

#### Style phrases that fit

- "Curious how you're thinking about…"
- "We're seeing a lot of [X] struggle with…"
- "Built [product] to solve exactly this. Fast and data-backed."
- "Thought I'd share, in case helpful."
- "No pressure, just figured this might be up your alley."

#### Examples (Katerina, UK / CEO profile)

**Example A**
```
Hi Lynn,
Circling back after connecting - curious how you're approaching user motivation without physical progress data. We're seeing more health platforms struggle with retention as GLP-1 users expect visible results.
At 3DLOOK we built FitXpress to give them that: precise body metrics and 3D progress tracking from the phone camera. How are you showing members progress between check-ins today?
Best,
Katerina
```

**Example B**
```
Hi Marissa,
As CEO of 3DLOOK, I've noticed a big shift: users now expect real proof of progress, not only numbers. We built FitXpress to give them body data and visuals from just two photos.
Could be a fit for MyFitnessPal. How do your users see their progress today?
Katerina
```

#### Notes

- Personalize the hook + observation **per contact**. They carry the personalization; the product intro stays stable.
- All numbers / claims still come from `proof-points.md`. Don't invent stats.
- Only the **opener style** follows this template. It does **not** override the brand no-go rules: no long dash, no triple parallelisms, no banned words. `brand-checker` fails a message that breaks them.

## Message 2 template (verbatim)

### Outbound - Message 2 Template & Style

> Source of truth for how `message-sequencer` writes **Message 2** of the 2-message company sequence.
> Message 2 is sent in **English** on LinkedIn **+5 days after Message 1**, and only when the prospect accepted the connection, received Message 1, and **did NOT reply**. (In Closely the sequence auto-stops on a reply, so this fires on silence only.)
> Set by Vadim, 2026-07-21.

#### Hard constraints

- **Language:** English.
- **Length:** ≤ **550 characters** total (greeting + body + link + signature, everything counted).
- **First person**, from the sending profile owner (Katerina / Nick / Olena / Kateryna / Vadim).
- **Signature:** first name only, **no title / role**.
- Output **only the message**. No subject line, no preamble, no commentary.
- **Short, honest, expert, conversational.**

#### Banned (hard FAIL, brand-checker enforces, CLAUDE.md §6), same as Message 1

- **No long dash of any kind (— or –).** Use a period, a comma, a colon, or a plain hyphen "-".
- **No triple parallelisms.** One or, at most, two concrete points.
- **No "It's not just X, it's Y"** (and avoid the casual "not just …" / "not only …" version too).
- **No banned words:** leverage, utilize, harness, robust, seamless, comprehensive, delve, navigate (figurative), tapestry, realm.
- **No generic AI openers, no clichés** ("I admire your mission", "excited about your journey").

#### Purpose

The follow-up after silence. **Lead with the value we can bring to them and their company**: a concrete outcome for their world, grounded in what we've seen in their vertical, not a feature list. Frame from experience and observation, not selling. Close with a **demo-call offer + calendar link** (the sending profile's own link). **Exception: the `vadim` profile has no calendar account, so instead of the demo-call offer + calendar link it closes with a short soft conversational ask (same style as Message 1: "Might be worth a quick chat?"), then the signature. No calendar link.**

#### Structure (in this order)

1. `Hi {first_name},` (a light re-touch is fine; this is a follow-up, keep it natural).
2. **One or two sentences of concrete value** for them / their company: the outcome we help with, tied to their vertical and the campaign hypothesis. This is the core of the message.
3. **Demo-call offer + calendar link** as **plain text** (the sending profile's link, from the table below). Keep the offer short ("Worth 15 min?", "Grab a slot:"). **`vadim` profile only: no calendar link. Replace this with a short soft conversational ask in Message 1 style ("Might be worth a quick chat?", "Open to a quick chat?", "Worth a quick chat to explore?"), then the signature.**
4. **Signature**: first name only.

#### Calendar links (per profile): use the SENDING profile's link

| profile | calendar link |
|---------|---------------|
| katerina | https://meetings.hubspot.com/katerina-galich |
| nick | https://meetings.hubspot.com/nick-omelchak |
| olena | https://meetings.hubspot.com/olena-kudriavtseva |
| katya | https://meetings.hubspot.com/kateryna-boichuk |
| vadim | **none — no calendar account. Use a soft ask instead of the CTA (see below).** |

**`vadim` has no calendar: write his Message 2 WITHOUT the demo-call offer and WITHOUT a calendar link. Instead close with a short soft conversational ask in Message 1 style ("Might be worth a quick chat?"), then the first-name signature (structure step 3).** For every other profile, insert its own link as plain text (no markdown, no shortener); never reuse another person's link, never invent one. If a listed link is ever blank/missing → STOP and ask Vadim.

#### Example (Katerina)
```
Hi Lynn,
Quick follow-up. Where we usually help platforms like yours: members stay engaged longer when they can see real body change between visits, so early GLP-1 drop-off softens. FitXpress adds that from a phone camera, straight into the member profile.
Worth 15 min to walk through it? Grab a slot here: https://meetings.hubspot.com/katerina-galich
Best,
Katerina
```

#### Notes

- Personalize the value line **per contact / vertical**. All numbers / claims come from `proof-points.md`; don't invent stats.
- Don't repeat Message 1 verbatim; this message earns the reply with value, then offers the call.
- Only the follow-up style follows this template; brand no-go rules and product accuracy (FitXpress vs Mobile Tailor) still apply.

## Output format

Write ONE file per batch, `messages/_batch-<batch>.md`, in exactly this shape:

    @@@ <person_id>
    hook: <the specific thing about this person or company the opener stands on>
    proof: <the fact cited, and its source file>
    --- M1
    Hi <first name>,

    <message 1>

    <signature>
    --- M2
    Hi <first name>,

    <message 2>

    <signature>

Then run `scripts/outbound_pack.py split-messages --campaign <slug> --in <that file>`.
It writes the per-person files, counts characters, runs the detector and every ban, and
prints ONLY what failed. Fix those entries in the batch file and run it again. Do not write
per-person files yourself, do not count characters yourself, do not run the detector
yourself.
